veranderings.voor: Ys smelt tot water en kookwater
veranderings.na: Ys smelt tot water, en kookwater
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses, each with its own subject and verb.
AWS comma: 'en' joins an imperative main clause to a clause with its own subject 'dit' and verb.
A three-item list reads more naturally with a comma than with a repeated 'of'.

veranderings.voor: Daar kom geen deeltjies by nie en geen
veranderings.na: Daar kom geen deeltjies by nie, en geen
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses, each with its own subject and verb.

veranderings.voor: Vaste plekke geld dus vir elke vaste stof.
veranderings.na: Elke vaste stof se deeltjies het dus vaste plekke.
veranderings.rede: 'Vaste plekke geld vir' is abstract and wooden; saying whose places they are is clearer and keeps the meaning.

veranderings.voor: 'n vaste plek nie en hulle sit
veranderings.na: 'n vaste plek nie, en hulle sit
veranderings.rede: AWS comma: 'en' joins two main clauses with different subjects ('geeneen' and 'hulle').

veranderings.na: In albei toestande is die deeltjies
veranderings.rede: 'albei' has no noun to refer to inside this block; naming the states makes the reference clear.

veranderings.na: teen mekaar of teen die wande
veranderings.rede: Repeating the preposition makes clear that the particles bump against the walls, not into 'each other or the walls' as one object.
AWS comma: 'en' joins an imperative main clause to a clause with its own subject 'die deeltjies' and verb; matches the parallel sentence in the second block.

veranderings.voor: vinnig genoeg beweeg by die oppervlak
veranderings.na: vinnig genoeg beweeg, by die oppervlak
veranderings.rede: A comma closing the relative clause separates the colliding verbs and stops 'beweeg by' being read as one verb.
The noun 'afkoeling' is the standard form as a sentence subject; a bare infinitive as subject reads colloquially.
